title: Pit viper bite with spreading swelling, 40-year-old plantation worker
provenance: Vignette written 2026-09-30 for the evaluation harness; expected answers extracted from the cited documents.

intake.complaint: Bitten on the right foot by a snake in an oil palm plantation 2 hours ago; the foot is swollen and painful and the bite marks keep bleeding.
intake.history: Snake described as brown with a triangular head; it was killed and brought in a bag. Swelling is spreading up to the ankle.

triage.note: Extractors disagreed (A 3, B 2); more urgent kept. A: The most urgent directly applicable MTS cells are Level 3. Adult Vital Signs Level 3 column (p7, x~244): 'Pain Score 4 - 7' (pain 7) and 'HR 100 - 120' (102). Primary triage Bleeding Level 3 column (p5, x~356): 'Bleeding from ... Wounds' and 'Bleeding Disorders' (bite marks keep bleeding). Level 2 is defensible for two reasons. (1) The MOH Snakebite guideline 2017 (p62) says patients with possible systemic and local envenomation go to the critical/red zone. (2) The MTS LETHARGY/WEAKNESS Level 2 cell (p10, x~131) lists 'Post exposure to drugs, bites, stings, toxins', but that row applies only if he is weak or lethargic, which the intake does not report. No L1/L2 bleeding cell (uncontrolled bleeding, compartment syndrome) is met. B: The MOH Snakebite guideline says to triage possible local or systemic envenomation to the critical/red zone. In MTS, the only Level 2 cell naming bites is 'Post exposure to drugs, bites, stings, toxins, environment' (x~131, p10), and it sits under the LETHARGY/WEAKNESS complaint, which this alert patient does not strictly have. The strictly applicable cells are all Level 3 (x~244): HR 102 and pain 7 (p7), and on p5 'Bleeding from ... Wounds' and 'Bleeding Disorders' (x~356 = Level 3 column there). So Level 2 is preferred, following the guideline and the most-urgent rule, and Level 3 is accepted.

adjudication.method: two independent extraction passes (A, B); agreed items scored
notes: Extractors disagreed (A 3, B 2); more urgent kept.

A: Triage L3 vs L2: MTS table cells give L3. The MOH Snakebite guideline sends possible local+systemic envenomation to the red zone (L1/L2). The adjudicator should decide which governs.

Antivenom at triage: the intake gives swelling 'up to the ankle' at 2 h (the local criterion is 'beyond the ankle within a few hours') and persistent bite-site bleeding (not yet documented as systemic bleeding or coagulopathy). The antivenom decision therefore depends on coagulation/platelet results or further spread. The gold requires 'assess indication and give when indicated' rather than unconditional antivenom.
The species label should wait for expert identification of the killed snake (guideline p52). Pit viper/Calloselasma is accepted as the working diagnosis given the description and location.
Forbidden-drug regex for hydrocortisone/antihistamine is limited to prophylactic use, because both are legitimately used to treat antivenom anaphylaxis.
B: MTS triage: the only Level 2 'bites' cell sits under LETHARGY/WEAKNESS. Level 2 rests on the MOH guideline's red-zone instruction; strictly applicable MTS cells give Level 3.

Does the antivenom indication already apply at presentation? Swelling has reached the ankle at 2 h ('rapid extension ... beyond the wrist or ankle within a few hours'), and the bite marks keep bleeding. That bleeding is local, not spontaneous systemic bleeding; the coagulation result will decide. Antivenom is marked required on the swelling criterion.
Tranexamic acid and vitamin K are called 'not effective', not 'avoid', so that forbidden item is non-required.
